newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Hongkong Bank NZ first half profit up sharply.
newsitem.headline: Hongkong Bank NZ first half profit up sharply.

text.p: The New Zealand branch of Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corp Ltd on Friday reported a sharp lift in operating profit to NZ$7.05 million in the six months to June 30 from $1.74 million a year earlier.

The bank, whose ultimate parent is HSBC Holdings Plc, said its capital adequacy rose to 9.8 percent from 9.1 percent and its ratio of total capital risk to weighted assets rose to 15.1 percent from 14.8 a year earlier.
Operating income, mostly from fees, rose to NZ$9.54 million from $7.06 million.
Residential mortgage business rose to NZ$341.16 million from $209.65 million.
Chief Executive John Blanthorne told Reuters in an interview the year-ago operating profit was low, mostly due to a loss incurred in the treasury and from heavy investment in personal banking.
Hongkong Bank NZ had been involved in some big transactions in the course of the year, resulting in significantly higher loan fees.

In the first half, Hongkong Bank NZ, in alliance with its HSBC's investment bank in Singapore, had arranged a US$225 million transferrable loan facility for Brierley Investments, consummated in the first half.
BIL had raised raised US$680 million since November 1994, much of it through Hongkong Bank.
The investment banking unit, working with HSBC makrets in Tokyo, had also arranged a 20 billion yen (NZ$260 million) placement for 10 years for BIL.
The investor was American Family Life Assurance.
"These types of transactions have obviously helped us generate increased investment banking income," Blanthorne said.
The issue was priced 100 basis points over the 10 year Japanese Government bond rate.

Hongkong Bank was one of three banks involved in the purchase by a Fletcher Challenge consortium of state owned Forestry Corp of New Zealand Ltd. Bank of New Zealand Ltd and Westpac Banking Corp were the other two.
Since June 30, the bank was maintaining the same level of performance. "So we are looking for a very good full year result," he said.

Blanthorne said Hongkong Bank now intended to grow its mortgage business outside Auckland, targetting Wellington initially, but had no long term ambitions to have a significant branch network. -- Wellington Newsroom (64-4-4734746)
